title: Does the Tauri app own the hub, or sit on top of it?
context: Decision 4 chose a Tauri window around the hub page with the Node server as a 'sidecar' (a child process the app owns). The plan (memo M028, researcher tauri-plan) found that a true sidecar fits badly: Tauri sidecars are standalone executables, so the Node hub and the Agent SDK would need packaging into one exe (fragile); the hub restarts itself, which slips out of Tauri's hold on it anyway; and quitting or crashing the window app would take the hub, and the phone's access, down with it. Either way the window loads the live hub at http://crux.localhost:4747, so decision 48's PC trust works unchanged, and the page gets no Tauri native access. The app lives in app/ in the crux repo (hub/ stays dependency-free). Build tools: Microsoft C++ Build Tools and Rust (about 9-12 GB, Matt's call). Amends decision 4.

options.name: Sit on top: attach to the hub, start it if it's down
options.summary: The app checks the hub at launch and starts it the usual way if it isn't running. Restarts (restart_hub, the menu, the tray) work as today. Quitting the app leaves the hub running, so the phone keeps working.
pros: Nothing about how the hub runs or restarts changes
The phone never loses the hub because the window closed or crashed
No packaging of Node or the Agent SDK
cons: Two things to think about (app and hub) instead of one

options.name: Own it: a true sidecar
options.summary: As decision 4 said: the app packages and starts the hub as its child, and quitting the app stops the hub.
pros: One thing to start and stop
cons: Packaging the Node hub and the Agent SDK into one exe is fragile
Self-restarts fight Tauri's hold on the process
Closing or crashing the app cuts off the phone

recommendation: A keeps everything that works today and only adds a window, a tray and PC notifications on top.

settles.value: Tauri window that loads the live local server's page and attaches to the server (starting it if down) rather than owning it; quitting the window leaves the server running
